Hello, I am considering buying a wi-fi adapter for my computer (desktop, prebuilt) as I would love to have my PC in my own room but at the same time; I don't want to waste good money so I am wondering if I should buy a wi-fi adapter, and which one would work best or if I should skip wi-fi adapters and go for a wireless card when I build my next PC.
USB wi-fi adapters, are they worth buying?

I bought one for an old junk heap and I know it worked... But the computer wouldn't be able to run anything anyways.

It really comes down to how you game. If you play online games I recommend card or even better Ethernet but if all you play is offline games that you're going to need to download then you could get by with a USB.

Depends on your expectations. WiFi is unreliable and not best for low latency applications. If you only need connection to your router due to physical limitations, WiFi is better than nothing.

Choosing adapters depend on your router (single/dual band). Get a matching adapter that supports what technology your router have. Drivers must explicitly state it supports your OS and version. At least 3x3 antenna.
Really depends on how you use your PC. Do you game or watch movies or basic social media activities?

G'day sir. I used a USB Wifi adapter for a while but it was quite bad. I bought a PCI-Wifi adapter (which should be more powerful than standard USB, difference is you fit it into a PCI slot inside computer) and the connection was still quite weak (slightly better tho'). I am a floor above my internet Hub. I then bought an ethernet extender, just plugged first part next to the Hub downstairs and the second part in my room, connected the second part to my PC using ethernet cable and... Blazing fast speeds.

Then again... On my laptop, the internet speed is good.

So what I learned from this: Ethernet>WifiCard>WifiPCI>WifiUSB

But then again, I might be wrong. Situational differences etc.

I have a cheap 5$ usb, and the connection to my router less than 20 feet away (separated by 1 wall) is a horrid 2-3 bars. It also completely drops the connection if someone turns on the microwave. In comparison, my laptop has a solid 5 bars, never once dropping, not even when the microwave is on.

The best thing you can do is buy a 50-100 foot Ethernet cable. They are actually really cheap if you buy online. Amazon Link
I bought one and used it for a year or so, you have to do what you have to do. Much less reliable than wired but never noticed significant bandwidth issues.

Get a Hawking HD65U

You wont be disappointed. I used an older HAWNU1 for years and it was exceptional for both range and quality of connection. The only thing better than a hawking adaptor is a wire.
Get this one - you won't regret it. http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B007GMPZ0A?psc=1&redirect=true&ref_=oh_aui_detailpage_o07_s01
No problem. But make sure to just plug and play and use the generic Windows drivers. Apparently the ones on the disk that comes with it are crap.

I have a Netgear A6210 (802.11ac) for my Laptop which goes up to 802.11n. I found the n to be unreliable and the n wasn't even an option to allow on my network card, it was more of "if it's available we might use it". It would also go to 2.4GHz even though I chose 5, so the Netgear fixes both of these. Honestly, any 5GHz band WiFi USB would work, but from the reviews and testing, it shows that the Netgear keeps it's strength of signal more than others and that's something I need. It's pretty damn fast for WiFi compared to my Ethernet connection. You could get a WiFi card as /u/DoNotTrustMe suggests, but Powerline Adapters may be an option as well. Ethernet over all if possible though.

Net gear are pretty popular, I'm using tp-link for my Ethernet extender.

But pretty much what /u/shneap is saying, Ethernet just destroys the competition.

Wired will always outperform wireless.
